Separating semantic recognition from spatial control is an architectural choice. CLIPort combines CLIP's semantic features with Transporter-style spatial processing <Cite id="clipport-2021" />. RoboFlamingo uses a vision-language model for each observation and a separate policy head for temporal history <Cite id="roboflamingo-2023" />. The representation objective matters too. Voltron balances language-conditioned image reconstruction with image-conditioned language generation to learn both spatial detail and semantics <Cite id="voltron-2023" />. LIV learns representations and goal-conditioned rewards from captioned videos without action labels <Cite id="liv-2023" />. CortexBench found no visual representation that won every task: VC-1 led on average, while adaptation to a task or domain brought further gains <Cite id="vc1-2023" />.

Spatial representations make different compromises. PerAct encodes RGB-D observations as voxels and predicts a discrete voxel action <Cite id="peract-2022" />. RVT renders virtual views around the workspace and aggregates them with attention <Cite id="rvt-2023" />. Act3D instead samples a 3D feature field from coarse to fine to focus computation where an action needs precision <Cite id="act3d-2023" />. GNFactor jointly trains a neural-field reconstruction module and a policy on shared 3D voxel features <Cite id="gnfactor-2023" />.

Luckcuck and colleagues find testing and simulation insufficient evidence for certifying autonomous robots <Cite id="luckcuck-formal-2019" />. Kalra and Paddock calculate that existing fleets would need tens and sometimes hundreds of years of driving to demonstrate autonomous-vehicle reliability <Cite id="kalra-paddock-2016" />, and [deployment numbers](/frontier/reliability-gap/) show the same distance.
edits.after:

Properties of a neural network can be checked in restricted settings. Reluplex extends the simplex method to ReLU activations and demonstrated property verification on prototype ACAS Xu aircraft collision-avoidance networks <Cite id="reluplex-2017" />.

edits.before: The formal instance is the safety filter. A <Term id="control-barrier-function">control barrier function</Term> defines a set the system must stay inside and turns forward invariance of that set into a constraint on the commanded input, enforced each step <Cite id="ames-cbf-2019" />. Wabersich and colleagues survey the family, including reachability and predictive variants, and describe a filter that takes a proposed input from any source and modifies it as little as necessary <Cite id="wabersich-safety-filters-2023" />.
edits.after:
The formal instance is the safety filter. A <Term id="control-barrier-function">control barrier function</Term> defines a set the system must stay inside and turns forward invariance of that set into a constraint on the commanded input, enforced each step <Cite id="ames-cbf-2019" />. Wabersich and colleagues survey the family, including reachability and predictive variants, and describe a filter that takes a proposed input from any source and modifies it as little as necessary <Cite id="wabersich-safety-filters-2023" />.

The mechanism varies with the specification. Ames and colleagues combine barrier constraints with Lyapunov performance objectives in a quadratic program <Cite id="cbf-qp-2016" />. A predictive filter instead checks a proposed input through model predictive control with state- and input-dependent uncertainty <Cite id="predictive-safety-filter-2018" />. A temporal-logic shield can restrict the available actions or correct one that violates its specification <Cite id="shielding-2017" />.

Runtime assurance can also switch controllers. Neural Simplex transfers control to a baseline when the neural controller proposes a potentially unsafe input, and adds retraining and a route back to the advanced controller <Cite id="neural-simplex-2019" />.

Learning a barrier still needs assumptions. Robey and colleagues learn one from safe expert trajectories for a known control-affine dynamical system, with guarantees under specified smoothness conditions <Cite id="learn-cbf-2020" />. CPO instead targets near-constraint satisfaction during policy optimization and tests safety-motivated constraints in simulated locomotion <Cite id="constrained-policy-2017" />.

edits.before: <Term id="conformal-prediction">Conformal prediction</Term> turns any model's raw output into a prediction set with a guaranteed coverage rate under exchangeability. Vovk, Gammerman and Shafer built the framework <Cite id="vovk-conformal-2022" />, and Angelopoulos and Bates's tutorial carried it into general machine-learning practice <Cite id="angelopoulos-conformal-2021" />. In KnowNo, Ren and colleagues calibrate a language-model planner conformally so that the robot asks a human for help when its prediction set is ambiguous, with a statistical guarantee on task completion <Cite id="knowno-2023" />.

Adaptive conformal inference tracks coverage over long time intervals as the data distribution changes <Cite id="adaptive-conformal-2021" />. These are aggregate statistical targets; none means every individual decision is correct.

<span id="start-with-the-intended-use" />
## Perception scores miss function, so each use needs its own test

WorldArena scores 14 models separately as data engines, policy evaluators and action planners, and reports a "significant perception-functionality gap" <Cite id="worldarena-2026" />. NVIDIA reports its DreamGen Bench video scores tracking downstream policy success <Cite id="dreamgen-2025" />. 1X saw unchanged policy weights degrade within days after subtle lighting or background changes <Cite id="1x-world-model-2024" />.

<span id="level-1-one-step-action-sensitivity" />
## Level 1: open models often fail to follow a changed action

Build matched counterfactuals: fix the observation, noise, prompt and history, and change one action dimension. WorldEval found raw action inputs often yield videos that ignore the action <Cite id="worldeval-2025" />, and IRASim and Ctrl-World add frame-level action conditioning <Cite id="irasim-2024" /> <Cite id="ctrl-world-2025" />. Across six open action-conditioned world models and more than 18,000 test instances, WorldSimProbe found systematic degradation in how actions are realized <Cite id="worldsimprobe-2026" />.

<span id="level-2-temporal-and-physical-consistency" />
## Level 2: pooled video metrics hide physical errors

Roll out autoregressively, score task events such as grasp, slip and release, and report error per horizon. Fréchet Video Distance "increases only slightly with large temporal corruption" <Cite id="fvd-content-bias-2024" />. WorldModelBench uses 67K human labels to catch violations such as objects changing size <Cite id="worldmodelbench-2025" />, and video models trained on simple physics failed out of distribution, copying the closest training example <Cite id="video-physical-law-2024" />.

<span id="level-3-task-progress-scoring" />
## Level 3: the progress scorer needs its own test

Many evaluators pair a video generator with a vision-language scorer, as WorldGym does, so each half needs its own test <Cite id="worldgym-2025" />. GVL fixes poor naive VLM value prediction by ordering shuffled frames, scoring more than 300 real tasks <Cite id="gvl-2024" />. Runway and DreamDojo used human graders instead, Runway collecting over 16,000 ratings <Cite id="runway-gwm-robotics-eval-2026" /> <Cite id="dreamdojo-2026" />.

<span id="level-4-policy-ranking" />
## Level 4: the best simulators order policies as real trials do

A policy evaluator must reproduce reality's ordering, measured as Pearson correlation and Mean Maximum Rank Violation (MMRV) <Cite id="runway-gwm-robotics-eval-2026" />. Real comparisons often rest on 10 to 50 trials, and adding trials after peeking risks p-hacking; the STEP sequential test cuts trials by up to 32% <Cite id="optimal-stopping-2025" />.

<Image id="roboarena-evaluation-2025" />

Google DeepMind reports its Veo simulator ranked eight Gemini Robotics checkpoints against more than 1,600 real evaluations at MMRV 0.03, though its absolute success predictions ran low <Cite id="veo-world-simulator-2025" />. Runway reports Pearson 0.95 and MMRV 0.033 over eight RoboArena policies, testing ranking only <Cite id="runway-gwm-robotics-eval-2026" />. PolaRiS found that Ctrl-World "produces heavy hallucinations during object interaction", mis-ranking policies at MMRV 0.22 <Cite id="polaris-2025" />.

Physics simulation sets the bar. In June 2026, Yuke Zhu and colleagues reported that SimFoundry, which rebuilds a real scene in simulation from video, predicted real results across 7 tasks and 5 policy architectures at mean Pearson 0.911 and MMRV 0.018 <Cite id="simfoundry-2026" />. PolaRiS reports r = 0.9 against real trials <Cite id="polaris-2025" />, and X2Real 0.84 <Cite id="x2real-2026" />.

<span id="level-5-closed-loop-usefulness" />
## Level 5: planning and fine-tuning in a world model improved outcomes

IRASim planning raised Push-T IoU from 0.637 to 0.961 <Cite id="irasim-2024" />, and fine-tuning on Ctrl-World's imagined successes raised policy success by 44.7% <Cite id="ctrl-world-2025" />.
